backend.title: feat: project registry and GitHub App installations
backend.body:
## Context

Ensemble follows several projects, each made of repositories where the platform's GitHub App is installed (A1 of the platform spec (`.scratch/platform/spec.md` in project-generator)). Every other feature reads this registry. Data model: `projects`, `repositories`, `app_installations` in the Architect's plan (`.scratch/platform/architecture.md`), section 5.

## User story

As the owner, I want Ensemble to know my projects and which repositories the App can see, so that every screen can be scoped to a project.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given an `installation` or `installation_repositories` webhook, when it arrives, then `app_installations` and `repositories` reflect the repositories the App can see, without duplicates.
- Given registered projects, when `GET /v1/projects` is called, then it returns each project with its repositories, kind and agent-team version, sorted by name.
- Given a repository without the App, when `GET /v1/account` is called, then it is listed as without access, with the App's install URL.
- Migrations follow the database naming of the conventions and only add.

## Contract changes

`GET /v1/projects`, `GET /v1/account` (registry part); the webhook endpoint itself is B3.

## UI

none (the frontend's app shell, F1, uses it)

## Out of scope

login (B2); webhook signature and the event log (B3).

## Blocked by

none

## Feature flag

none

## Idempotency key

not needed

backend.title: feat: login with GitHub through the platform's App
backend.body:
## Context

Only the owner's GitHub account may enter (A2), and every write to GitHub is done as the user with the App's user-to-server token (A1). Contract: *Auth and access* in the Architect's plan (`.scratch/platform/architecture.md`), section 6; risk R3 (single-use refresh tokens).

## User story

As the owner, I want to sign in with GitHub and stay signed in, so that Ensemble can act on GitHub as me.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a visitor, when `GET /v1/auth/github/start` is called, then it redirects to GitHub with a `state` kept in a short-lived signed cookie.
- Given GitHub's callback with a valid `state`, when the user is the owner (`OWNER_GITHUB_LOGIN`, pinned to its id at first login), then the token is stored encrypted, the `session` and `logged_in` cookies are set and the browser goes to the app.
- Given another GitHub account, when the callback arrives, then no session is opened and the answer is `AUTH_NOT_OWNER`; a wrong `state` gives `AUTH_STATE_INVALID`.
- Given an expired access token, when two requests refresh it at once, then the refresh happens once, inside a row lock on `github_credentials`.
- Given a refresh GitHub refuses, when any request needs the token, then the session ends with `SESSION_EXPIRED`.
- Every `/v1` route except the public ones (`/v1/auth/*`, `/v1/webhooks/github`, `/v1/dispatcher-events`, `/v1/client-errors`, `/v1/display-pairings` start) requires the session and answers `UNAUTHENTICATED` without it.

## Contract changes

the auth endpoints of the plan's section 6; `ErrorCode`s `AUTH_STATE_INVALID`, `AUTH_NOT_OWNER`, `SESSION_EXPIRED`, `UNAUTHENTICATED`. New ADR in both repositories: GitHub App login and acting as the user (D3).

## UI

none (F1 builds the login screen)

## Out of scope

the TV pairing (B8).

## Blocked by

none

## Feature flag

none

## Idempotency key

not needed

backend.title: feat: event log and GitHub webhook ingestion
backend.body:
## Context

Everything the screens show comes from an append-only event log (A3), fed first by GitHub webhooks, processed in the request and idempotent by delivery id (A4, D9).

## User story

As the owner, I want every change on my repositories recorded once, so that the screens are right even when GitHub sends a delivery twice.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a delivery with a valid `X-Hub-Signature-256`, when `POST /v1/webhooks/github` receives it, then one `events` row is written with `dedupe_key` `github:<X-GitHub-Delivery>` and the answer is `204` in under a second.
- Given the same delivery again, when it arrives, then no new row is written and the answer is still `204`.
- Given a wrong signature, when it arrives, then the answer is `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID` (401) and nothing is written.
- Given the `events` table, when any code tries to update or delete a row, then there is no repository method to do it.
- Each write sends `NOTIFY ensemble_events, <seq>`.

## Contract changes

`POST /v1/webhooks/github`; `ErrorCode` `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID`. New ADR: the event log and projection.

## UI

none

## Out of scope

the projection (B5) and the stream (B6).

## Blocked by

B1

## Feature flag

none

## Idempotency key

the delivery id (`X-GitHub-Delivery`) through `uq_events_dedupe_key`

backend.title: feat: dispatcher events ingestion
backend.body:
## Context

The agent-team dispatcher can POST every decision it takes to `events-url` (agent-team v0.3.0). Each repository gets its own token.

## User story

As the owner, I want the dispatcher's decisions in the same log as GitHub's events, so that the screens know what the team did and why.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a repository, when the owner issues its events token, then only its SHA-256 hash is stored and the token is shown once.
- Given a body with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` of the same repository, when `POST /v1/dispatcher-events` receives it, then one event is written with `dedupe_key` `dispatcher:<sha256 of body>` and the answer is `204`.
- Given a token of another repository, or none, then the answer is `EVENTS_TOKEN_INVALID` (401); an unknown repository gives `REPOSITORY_NOT_REGISTERED` (404).
- Given the same body twice, then one event is written.

## Contract changes

`POST /v1/dispatcher-events`; `ErrorCode`s `EVENTS_TOKEN_INVALID`, `REPOSITORY_NOT_REGISTERED`.

## UI

none (the token is issued from the health screen, B14 and F9)

## Out of scope

asking agent-team to add an event id (noted in the plan).

## Blocked by

B1, B3

## Feature flag

none

## Idempotency key

the SHA-256 of the body

backend.title: feat: projection of tickets and agent runs
backend.body:
## Context

The screens read a projection built from the events: each ticket's stage, flags and returns, and each agent run (A3).

## User story

As the owner, I want each ticket's current state computed from what happened, so that every screen agrees.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given the events of a ticket, when they are projected, then `tickets` has its stage, labels, `is_escalated`, `is_stalled`, `is_queued`, `is_awaiting_ok`, `returns_count` and `last_event_seq`.
- Given label events for a role, then `agent_runs` records when it started and ended.
- Given `serve projection:rebuild`, when it runs, then the projection is truncated and replayed and ends equal to what it was.
- The agent states (working, waiting for you, queued, stalled, free) are computed, never stored.

## Contract changes

none

## UI

none

## Out of scope

reconciliation with GitHub (B11).

## Blocked by

B3, B4

## Feature flag

none

## Idempotency key

not needed

backend.title: feat: live updates over SSE
backend.body:
## Context

The live screens and the team wall update through Server-Sent Events (T3), woken by PostgreSQL `LISTEN/NOTIFY` with replay from the log (D2). Stream contract in the Architect's plan (`.scratch/platform/architecture.md`), section 6.

## User story

As the owner, I want the screens to update by themselves, so that I never refresh to see what the team did.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a signed-in user, when `GET /v1/stream` is opened, then it answers `text/event-stream` with `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, an `id:` equal to the event `seq` and a `: ping` every 15 s.
- Given `Last-Event-ID`, when the stream reconnects, then every event after it is replayed before the live ones.
- Given five minutes open, then the stream ends with `retry: 2000`; given the browser leaving, then its goroutine ends.
- One hub per process holds the `LISTEN` connection; a test opens and closes streams and checks no subscriber is left (risk R2).
- Events are hints: `ticket.changed`, `agent.changed`, `notification.changed`, `pause.changed`, `activity.appended`.

## Contract changes

`GET /v1/stream`. New ADR in both repositories: live updates with SSE.

## UI

none (F2 consumes it)

## Out of scope

the wall's filtered stream (B8).

## Blocked by

B2, B5

## Feature flag

none

## Idempotency key

not needed

backend.title: feat: decisions and the actions taken as the user
backend.body:
## Context

Decisions gathers everything waiting for the owner, and the actions run on GitHub as the user (A1, F1, F8).

## User story

As the owner, I want one list of what waits for me and buttons that act for me on GitHub, so that I lead the team from any screen.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given supervised hand-offs, `spec-ready` tickets, escalations, dependency fixes and merges, when `GET /v1/decisions` is called, then each comes with its project, both sides' evidence for escalations, and `canOk`, `canMerge`, `canTieBreak`.
- Given a hand-off waiting, when `POST /v1/tickets/{id}/ok` is called, then a `/ok` comment is posted as the user.
- Given a pull request ready, when `/merge` is called, then it is squash-merged as the user; when not allowed, `TICKET_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` (409).
- Given an escalation, when `/tie-break {winner}` or `/retry` is called, then the decision comment and labels follow F8 (the stage is restored and the return count resets).
- GitHub down gives `GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE` (502); a repository without the App gives `REPOSITORY_NO_ACCESS` (403).

## Contract changes

`GET /v1/decisions`, `POST /v1/tickets/{id}/ok|merge|tie-break|retry`.

## UI

none (F3)

## Out of scope

the ticket screen (B13).

## Blocked by

B2, B5; F8's retry needs the agent-team dispatcher to restore the stage (open in agent-team)

## Feature flag

none

## Idempotency key

not needed

backend.title: feat: team wall displays and pairing
backend.body:
## Context

The TV never signs in with GitHub: it shows a code the owner confirms, and gets a display token that only reads the wall (A3, login decisions).

## User story

As the owner, I want to put the team wall on a TV with a short code, so that the team is visible without my GitHub login on the TV.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a TV, when `POST /v1/display-pairings` is called, then it answers `201` with `{pairingId, code, expiresAt}`, rate-limited.
- Given the owner signed in, when `POST /v1/display-pairings/confirm {code, name}` is called, then the pairing is confirmed and the TV's next `GET /v1/display-pairings/{id}` sets the `display` cookie once.
- Given a display token, when `GET /v1/wall` or `GET /v1/wall/stream` is called, then counters, roles, unread notifications and titles come back, never comment bodies.
- Given `DELETE /v1/displays/{id}`, then that TV gets `DISPLAY_TOKEN_REVOKED` at once.
- Only hashes of the codes and tokens are stored (D5).

## Contract changes

the display endpoints of the plan's section 6. New ADR in both repositories: TV display access.

## UI

none (F4)

## Out of scope

more than the wall for a display token.

## Blocked by

B2, B6

## Feature flag

## Idempotency key

backend.title: feat: PM chat through the scheduled task API trigger
backend.body:
## Context

The PM chat comments on the issue as the user and starts the PM's scheduled task through its API trigger (P1a, P1b, F2). Risk R5: the `/fire` request shape must be confirmed with the owner first.

## User story

As the owner, I want to talk to the PM from Ensemble, so that ideas become tickets without opening GitHub.

## Acceptance criteria

- Before any code: the `/fire` URL, headers and body are confirmed with the owner in a comment.
- Given the PM task's URL and token, when `PUT /v1/scheduled-tasks/{id}/api-trigger` is called, then both are stored encrypted.
- Given a message for an issue, when `POST /v1/pm-chat/{projectId}/messages` is called, then it is commented as the user and the PM task is fired naming the issue; with no issue, a `needs-spec` issue is created first.
- Given no trigger stored, the answer is `ROUTINE_TRIGGER_NOT_CONFIGURED` (409); a failed `/fire` is `ROUTINE_TRIGGER_FAILED` (502) and is never retried automatically.

## Contract changes

the two PM chat endpoints of the plan's section 6.

## UI

backend.title: feat: scheduler process and the 15-minute reconciliation
backend.body:
## Context

A second command of the same binary runs the timed jobs in its own container (A4, D8); the first is the reconciliation that compares the projection with GitHub.

## User story

As the owner, I want Ensemble to repair what it missed, so that a lost webhook never leaves a screen wrong.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given `server scheduler`, when it starts, then it never migrates and runs each job inside `pg_try_advisory_lock`, so two never overlap.
- Given a ticket whose GitHub state differs from the projection, when the reconciliation runs, then it writes a correcting event with `dedupe_key` `reconciliation:<repo>:<number>:<hash>`.
- Every run is recorded in `job_runs` with its result.
- `docker-compose.prod.yml` gains the `scheduler` service with the same image and `command: ["scheduler"]`.

## Contract changes

none. New ADR: the scheduler container, an exception to the in-process scheduler ban.

## UI

none

## Out of scope

the quota probe and the digest (B15, B12).

## Blocked by

B5

## Feature flag

none

## Idempotency key

not needed

backend.title: feat: notifications
backend.body:
## Context

Notifications live in the platform only, no push (M2): a counter, a list with filters, one per event, replaced while unread, read when resolved; plus the optional daily digest.

## User story

As the owner, I want to see what waits for me in one list, so that I never miss a decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given pending decisions, escalations, stalls, quota pauses and merges, when they happen, then one notification each is created, and a newer one for the same ticket and kind replaces an unread older one.
- Given `GET /v1/notifications?filter=&kind=&page=&size=`, then the list is paginated with the unread count; `POST /v1/notifications/read-all` marks them read.
- Given the thing resolved (decided, `/ok`, merged), then its notification is read on every screen through `notification.changed`.
- Pending decisions, escalations, stalls and quota cannot be turned off; merge and digest can.

## Contract changes

the notification endpoints of the plan's section 6.

backend.title: feat: probable quota pause and probe
backend.body:
## Context

The platform cannot read the subscription quota, so it infers it (M4): 3 stalls of different roles or tickets in 30 minutes pause new starts, hold the retries, and a probe every 30 minutes releases one ticket.

## User story

As the owner, I want the team to stop wasting retries when the quota is out, so that work resumes cleanly when it is back.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given 3 stalls of different roles or tickets within 30 minutes, then a quota pause starts, new starts stop and every screen gets `pause.changed` with reason `quota`.
- Given a pause, when 30 minutes pass, then the scheduler releases one stalled ticket as a probe with the user's token (D4); a verdict ends the pause and the stalled tickets return one at a time without counting a retry.
- Given `POST /v1/quota/resume {reason}`, then `quota` resumes now and `not-quota` treats the stalls as usual.

## Contract changes

`POST /v1/quota/resume`.

## UI

none (F10)

## Out of scope

reading the quota from claude.ai.

## Blocked by

B9, B11; the probe needs the dispatcher's pause (open in agent-team)

## Feature flag

none

## Idempotency key

not needed
